# Research results

## Research questions

| Number | Question, as in the proposal | Endpoint | Method | Null hypothesis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Do measurements from the first antenatal visit improve prediction of recorded low birth weight beyond the second visit alone in the eligible cohort? | Average precision of set C minus set B | Paired group bootstrap, both model families; the prespecified primary hypothesis | Adding first visit values changes average precision by zero |
| 2 | Does a learned model outperform constant prevalence prediction, and does adding the earlier visit improve both discrimination and calibration over the second visit features alone? | Average precision of sets A, B and C minus the prevalence only model; ROC AUC, Brier score, calibration slope and intercept of set C minus set B | Paired group bootstrap; DeLong's test beside each ROC AUC as descriptive | Each difference is zero |
| 3 | Optionally, within fixed ranking budgets, what proportion of pregnancies subsequently recorded as low birth weight is retrieved by model ranking relative to ranking at random? | Share of events in the top 10, 20 and 30 percent of the served ranking, minus the share random ranking retrieves | Group bootstrap of retrieval minus the random expectation | The served ranking retrieves no more than random |
| 4 | What sensitivity do the feature set comparisons show to missing measurements and to questionable outcome records? | The primary comparison, C minus B average precision, under each sensitivity analysis, and missingness indicators added to sets B and C | Paired group bootstrap; saved sensitivity analyses use the normal approximation | Each difference is zero |

## Results on development records

Pooled out of fold predictions averaged over 10 repeats, 3,126 records with 165 events. Each interval is a paired group bootstrap with 2,000 resamples; p is twice the smaller share of resamples on either side of zero. The primary hypothesis (question 1) and the prespecified secondary hypothesis (set B over set A on ROC AUC) are not adjusted; every other tested row is one exploratory family with a Holm adjustment. DeLong's test ignores registration groups and is descriptive only. No test is made over fold level results. A p value marked * comes from a saved sensitivity analysis on another cohort, whose predictions are not stored, and uses the normal approximation with its saved bootstrap standard error.
